issues.issue: Decision 1's recommended option B contradicts both R1 verdicts' mitigations. B keeps the Spotify provider in FXM's repo and builds (off by default) and has FXM's own code fetch the TOTP secret list from a pre-filled community gist. R1 verdict 1: 'FXM must never host or fetch the TOTP secrets itself.' R1 verdict 2: keep Spotify 'out of the FXM core and out of the FXM owner's hands: an optional plugin in a separate repo with a different maintainer', and 'never host or publish TOTP secrets from anything FXM controls'. The precedents point the same way: the 2025-10-10 letter targeted a TOTP-secret source (spotify-secrets, now 404), and the 2026-10-15 Echo letter demanded the developer 'forever desist' from reverse engineering any Spotify software and from aiding others (it also cited s.1201 and the Lanham Act; that extension also decrypted audio, so the fit is partial). Default-off does not change what FXM distributes, and pre-filling the gist URL is the 'aiding' those letters name. The owner-hosted remote config also carries Spotify operation hashes. The memo dismisses C as 'mostly cosmetic under the same owner' but never presents the verdict-backed variant, an independent maintainer, as an option.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite Decision 1 so the owner sees the verdict-backed option: the provider in a separate repo with an independent maintainer, loaded only from a URL the user enters, with no Spotify code, hashes or secret URLs in FXM or its remote config. If B stays: (1) build official release artifacts with the Spotify flag off and let the owner enable it in local builds; (2) ship no pre-filled secret source (the user pastes one); (3) state in the decision text that B does not lower letter risk; (4) add the Echo letter's demands to the risk row. If C is chosen, state that M1 ships without Spotify, and specify how plugin code loads under the strict CSP and under F-Droid's opt-in rule for downloaded executables.

issues.issue:
The 2.8 header spec would break tiers the memo promises, and its done-when would not catch it.
(a) 'media-src https://*.googlevideo.com blob:' blocks Internet Archive and Jamendo audio, which is the whole Free-only tier and the 'prefer lossless' path. It also blocks user-entered Invidious audio (rung 7, served from arbitrary hosts). connect-src lists neither the Spotify secret-source host nor any user-entered host. No img-src is given for ytimg, googleusercontent, i.scdn.co or the Cover Art Archive redirects to archive.org. ffmpeg.wasm needs 'wasm-unsafe-eval'.
(b) Cloudflare Pages applies the headers of every matching _headers rule and joins duplicate header values with commas (docs updated 2026-08-25). A /app/* CSP plus a /app/sandbox/* CSP therefore reach the sandbox pages as two policies, both enforced. eval.html's 'unsafe-eval' is then blocked unless the sandbox rules detach the parent CSP with '! Content-Security-Policy'.
Pages also limits a site to 100 header rules and each header line to 2,000 characters. The 2.8 done-when only checks YouTube playback.
issues.suggestion: Replace the prose with a per-path header table: /app/*, /app/sandbox/innertube.html, /app/sandbox/eval.html and /embed/*, using '! Content-Security-Policy' wherever a rule overrides a broader one. Add https://archive.org, https://*.archive.org and Jamendo's storage hosts to media-src, an img-src for the artwork CDNs, and 'wasm-unsafe-eval' where ffmpeg.wasm runs. Decide explicitly whether user-entered hosts (Invidious, the secret source) are supported on the web, for example via 'media-src https:' only, or dropped there. Extend the 2.8 done-when: an Internet Archive track and a Jamendo track play on the deployed site, eval.html can evaluate, and innertube.html cannot fetch outside its three hosts.

issues.issue: The ISRC gate contradicts the matching verdicts and can produce confident wrong Auto plays. The memo widens the gate from result #1 to the top 5 but keeps 'title similarity >= 0.5 OR artist similarity >= 0.5', and any accepted hit counts as 'ISRC-verified', which goes straight to Auto. Both matching F1 verdicts, and the spotube-audio F10 verdict, say to accept a hit only when title, artist and duration all match ('an ATV whose artist matches and whose title and duration also match'; 'accept it only if title AND artist AND duration (about ±4 s) all match'). The verdicts also found ISRCs shared by unrelated tracks (GBAYE0601696 maps to a Waw*mart track; QMFMF2447070 maps to 'You and me' by Lil dexxy), and found that ISRC misses return unrelated ATV filler. With OR across five slots, a same-title cover or squatter near the right length, or another song by the same artist, passes and auto-plays.
issues.suggestion: Require artist >= 0.5 AND |Δduration| <= max(5 s, 2 %) AND no strong version mismatch for every ISRC hit. Allow the title test to be skipped only for item #1 when the scripts differ (the アイドル case); send anything else that fails to Suggest. Add squatter, cover and same-artist-filler fixtures to 1.7's golden set and to 1.12.

issues.issue: The re-recording guard does not cover the failure it is meant to fix. It fires only when two or more same-title, same-artist candidates from different releases appear on the page. In the held-out 'The Twist' case, neither true recording (ABKCO or TEEC) was in the top 5 (F4 empirical verdict), so a lone wrong-release candidate can still auto-play. The guard was never replayed against the three cited failures. Its 'Provided to YouTube by' label input needs an extra /player or /next call per candidate, and that cost is not in the request budget.
issues.suggestion:
Add cheap rules that don't depend on rivals being present:
(a) If an ISRC is known but the gate misses after its retry and top-card check, cap text matches at Suggest. The miss suggests YouTube Music lacks that master (Spotify Singles, compilation-only ISRCs). Measure the Auto-rate cost in 1.12.
(b) When metadata/4 gives a label and release date, demote candidates whose album year or 'Provided to YouTube by' label contradicts them.
(c) In 1.7, replay The 1975, The Twist and Bye Bye Love from recorded fixtures with the ISRC step off, and require Suggest.
(d) Budget the description fetches.

issues.issue: The memo's central playback rule cannot be met in the Lite tier. Sections 2.3 and 4.2 say to play only URLs that passed an end-of-file ranged GET, and 'Probe before playing' is listed as a rule on every rung. In Lite, neither the page nor the opaque-origin sandbox can read googlevideo responses: there is no ACAO for a foreign origin or for null, so a no-cors fetch is opaque and its status unreadable. The Lite ladder (VISIONOS, then itag 18) therefore cannot be probe-gated. Recovery keyed on 401/403/410 is also impossible with <audio src>, which reports only a MediaError or a stall. Implemented literally, Lite either never plays or quietly skips the safety check.
issues.suggestion: Write an explicit Lite exception into 2.3 and 1.10. In Lite, skip the byte probe and treat a MediaError or stall on the first request as the probe result: capped URLs failed within about 70–300 ms in the verdicts. Then fall back to itag 18 and re-resolve. Keep HTTP-status rules only where bytes are readable (Connect, desktop, Android). Add a 1.10 mock test where the VISIONOS URL is capped and the player falls back.

issues.issue: The sandbox documents are opaque only when FXM itself frames them with sandbox="allow-scripts". Any site can frame /app/sandbox/innertube.html or eval.html without that attribute, and they then run with the real FXM origin. For a visitor with FXM Connect, Connect's DNR rules (initiatorDomains fxm-music.pages.dev) then rewrite Origin and add ACAO, so innertube.html becomes an attacker-controlled YouTube API proxy on the visitor's IP. The 1.10 design checks only 'event.source on one side and the parent on the other', and in this case the parent is the attacker. eval.html would evaluate whatever code its parent sends, inside the FXM origin.
issues.suggestion: Serve both sandbox documents with a 'Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts' response header, so they are opaque however they are loaded and Connect's rules never match them. Inside the sandbox, accept messages only when event.origin is the FXM origin. Do not rely on frame-ancestors 'self': it checks every ancestor, so it would break 5.2's Lite fallback when the FXM embed is itself framed by a third-party site. Add these checks to the 1.10 and 1.11 done-when.

issues.issue:
The TL;DR, §2.1 and §2.4 claim verification the reports do not show.
- Lite: in browsers, only /search and /player ran from a sandbox. Radio and /browse with Origin null were checked only with curl and Node. The VISIONOS 'resolved and played' result is Edge playing 0.66 s; the Chrome run played an IOS URL, which is a capped client. Every playback test stopped at 64 KB, Firefox never reached 'playing', and Safari/iOS were not tested.
- Desktop: 'Verified in … Tauri on macOS 15.5' is wrong for playback. No stream was ever resolved through plugin-http (run6 had streaming_data undefined). Now Playing, media keys and the 7-minute hidden playback were measured in a Swift WKWebView harness, not in Tauri. WebView2 and WebKitGTK were never run.
- Android: source reading only. 6.3 states as fact that the foreground service keeps WebView JS re-resolution working, which is an inference.
So 'Feasible on every platform … including a no-install Lite tier' is unsupported. The risk row also understates losing Lite ('Medium'): for iOS and Chrome-on-Android users, and for embed visitors, Lite is the only ad-free path.
issues.suggestion:
Relabel the claims, for example 'verified for the first 64 KB in Chromium' and 'components verified separately on macOS'. Add done-when items:
- 1.10: a full-length manual Lite playback in Chromium and Firefox, and Safari if available.
- 7.2/7.3: a full-track VISIONOS playback through plugin-http in the Tauri app.
- 6.3: playback that survives the WebView renderer being killed or the 2–3-item queue running out, using a deeper resolved queue (URLs last about 6 h) or a native resolver fallback.
Rate the impact of losing Lite as High for mobile web and embeds.

issues.issue:
§11 misdescribes the in-progress work it modifies.
- feat/1.1-core-model is not empty. It has 9 commits and 3,124 added lines (2026-10-25 20:24 +0530) and already defines NetworkCapabilities { youtube: boolean; spotify: boolean; ... } and AudioCandidate.evidence: string[]. The memo's 1.1 change (tri-state unions, structured evidence fields) is therefore breaking, not 'additive'. Its 'off' | 'anonymous' | 'account' also conflates 'the user turned Spotify off' with 'this platform can't reach Spotify'.
- feat/1.9 rewrites Origin on every InnerTube request, not 'only on googlevideo preflights', and it hard-codes PRODUCTION_ORIGINS = ['https://fxm-music.pages.dev'].
- develop has moved to 97fe265, which rewrote 2.6 and 4.1 after the memo's 7eaac4e baseline.
issues.suggestion: Rebase §11 on 97fe265. Amend 1.1 explicitly before it merges: youtube: 'none' | 'simple' | 'full'; a Spotify reachability value separate from the user's on/off setting; and a new structured field (for example signals: {isrcVerified, releaseId, releaseYear, label, sourceAlbumMatch}) next to evidence: string[]. List the downstream stages that consume these types. Correct the 1.9 description; the mirror issue below means 1.9 does need a change.

issues.issue:
The 'second static host' mitigation (R.4, 2.8, risk register) fails where it would matter.
- FXM Connect serves only fxm-music.pages.dev: its origin list, content-script matches and DNR initiatorDomains are fixed at build time. A mirror would get only the Lite and Free tiers until users install a new extension, which for unpacked Chromium installs means a manual re-download.
- PWA libraries are tied to the origin.
- Desktop and Android fetch the remote config from a single URL.
- GitHub Pages, the obvious free mirror, cannot set response headers, so the per-document CSPs and the sandbox protections would be lost.
- The remote config is unsigned. A hijacked or re-registered site, or a leaked CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, could push a config that disables or reorders rungs in every installed app. This is the weakness the memo faults in Bloomee.
- R.4 names no mirror or Git host (Codeberg would not qualify, since it is German) and lists no owner accounts or secrets.
issues.suggestion: Choose the mirror origin now and add it to Connect's PRODUCTION_ORIGINS before the first extension release, which means 1.9 needs a change. Pick a mirror host that supports per-path headers. Have desktop and Android try a list of config URLs. Sign the config (ed25519/minisign, public key in each build, reject unsigned or older versions). In R.4, name the Git mirror (for example GitLab.com) and the static mirror, list the owner actions and secrets, and require in the done-when that the mirror passes the same playback test as 2.8.

issues.issue: Bulk pacing exceeds the YouTube budget the memo itself cites. §4.4 quotes about 300 videos, or about 1,000 webpage/player requests, per hour per guest session. §6.3 and §3.5 pace imports at about 1 request per second, which is roughly 3,600 per hour, with up to 4 calls per track. Imports, the 1.12 recorder (over 1,000 requests) and playback all share the user's IP and visitor session. Hitting the limit brings LOGIN_REQUIRED for VISIONOS on that IP ('Restricted IPs hit bot checks', yt-dlp #17904), so a 100–1,000-track import can break the user's own playback. Shared CGNAT IPs, common on Indian mobile networks, make this worse. None of it is listed as a failure mode.
issues.suggestion: Define one hourly InnerTube budget shared by matching and resolution, for example at most 600 calls per hour, with bulk work spaced at least 5 s apart. Give playback priority over imports. Pause bulk work on the first LOGIN_REQUIRED or 429 and resume it later, and make imports resumable. Apply the same pacing to the 1.12 recorder, and add a test for it.

issues.issue: §6.1 step 0 deletes and re-matches any cached match 'that fails to resolve'. But resolution also fails for reasons that have nothing to do with the match: VISIONOS closed for everyone, LOGIN_REQUIRED on the user's IP, being offline, or a 403 after an IP change. In each case good matches get deleted (pins too, unless explicitly protected), and re-match requests pile onto an IP that may already be flagged. Separately, URLs are cached per videoId until close to expiry and never flushed when the network or IP changes (Wi-Fi to cellular, a VPN toggle), so every cached URL returns 403 after a switch.
issues.suggestion: Delete or re-match only on video-level signals: UNPLAYABLE or ERROR for that videoId (removed, region-blocked) while other videos still resolve. Keep matches through ladder, network or bot-check failures, and never auto-delete pins. Key the URL cache by network and flush it on online, offline or connection-change events. Add these cases to 2.3's fake-clock tests.

issues.issue:
Matching inputs for the Spotify-off default (Decision 1 B) are mis-specified.
- Step 2 says to take the ISRC 'from MusicBrainz /ws/2/isrc ... found 14 of 15'. That endpoint looks recordings up by ISRC, so it cannot supply an ISRC for a title and artist, and the '14 of 15' figure measured coverage of ISRCs already known. Finding an ISRC by MusicBrainz recording search is fuzzy: score-100 ties put live, compilation and soundtrack versions first (F6 verdicts). Feeding such an ISRC into the gate produces an 'ISRC-verified' Auto play of the wrong recording.
- 3.6 makes Spotify's 'Download your data' JSON a first-class import with Spotify off, but that export has song, artist and album names (and library URIs) with no duration or ISRC, per Spotify's support page. The Auto band needs |Δ| <= max(5 s, 2 %), so it can never be reached and the duration term is undefined.
- 1.12 measures only the Spotify-on path.
issues.suggestion:
Specify two MusicBrainz paths:
- Exact: a lookup of the Spotify track URL through MusicBrainz URL relationships. This may count as ISRC-verified.
- Fuzzy: a recording search with a duration window and a most-releases preference. This is a hint only and never confers Auto.
Define a no-duration matching mode capped at Suggest for data-export imports. Add a Spotify-off slice (data-export JSON and MusicBrainz inputs) to 1.12.

issues.issue: Requirement 1 hinges on a single pseudonymous gist, and the memo gives no working way to fetch it on the web. Whether the page can read the default source over CORS was not measured. The stated fallback, 'the platform transport fetches it', does not exist on the web: Connect has no rule for gist hosts, a user-entered source can't have a static DNR rule, and the memo says the config 'can never add hosts'. 2.8's connect-src also omits the host. This third-party file is the primary dependency for all Spotify use, not a fallback, and a similar source (spotify-secrets) vanished after a letter.
issues.suggestion: Measure CORS on gist.githubusercontent.com now. If it is open, allow exactly that host in the CSP. If not, add a fixed, allowlisted secret URL to Connect's bridge, or let users paste the secret JSON, which also helps the legal posture. Specify the failure UX (Spotify paused, how to enter a new source) and cover it in 1.5's fixtures.

issues.issue: Desktop and Android only hot-update the data config. Code fixes, such as adding a client (VISIONOS needed youtubei.js 18.0.0) or changing a parser, still need an app release and a user install. That is exactly why stable Spotube stayed broken for months. On Android, once the 2027 rollout arrives, an unregistered APK needs 'Install anyway' for every update, and updates fail if the advanced flow is off. Breakage detection is weak too: the 'resolve and probe' self-test that 'CI runs behind FXM_LIVE=1' would run from GitHub-hosted datacenter IPs, where VISIONOS hits bot checks. CI would go red for the wrong reason, and green would prove little.
issues.suggestion: Ship the YouTube resolver (youtubei.js glue, client ladder, parsers) as a versioned, signed JS module served from the static site, with the bundled copy as a fallback. Desktop and Android load it after checking a signature against a key compiled into the app. Make this opt-in in F-Droid builds, because F-Droid forbids downloaded executables without opt-in consent, and disable self-update there. Treat CI live runs as advisory, and run the live smoke test on a schedule from a residential connection.

issues.issue: Missing failure mode: Mozilla can disable FXM Connect remotely. AMO policies apply to add-ons 'regardless of how they are distributed', and self-distributed XPIs still need AMO signing. One complaint from Google or Spotify could get the add-on ID blocklisted, disabling Connect for every Firefox user on desktop and Android. The memo makes AMO the primary extension channel, plans a listed submission that includes the cookie-reading Spotify session bridge, and has no risk row for this; its register covers only Chrome and Edge.
issues.suggestion: Add a risk row (likelihood low–medium, impact high for Firefox users). Consider a Firefox build without the Spotify bridge, or a separate bridge add-on, so a Spotify complaint cannot take down YouTube access. Have onboarding detect a disabled or blocked Connect and point users to the desktop app or the APK.

issues.issue:
The new stages have dependency and scope defects.
- 1.2 routes InnerTube 'else to the 1.10 sandbox' and its done-when tests three tiers, but 1.10 depends on 1.2: a cycle.
- 1.11's scope includes packages/player/src/engines/mse/**, but it doesn't depend on 2.2, which defines the engine interface.
- 1.11's done-when ('206 for a range in the last 64 KB of the file') can't apply to the SABR rung, which streams over UMP POSTs and has no file URL.
- eval.html is isolated by a per-document CSP from Cloudflare _headers. Tauri and Capacitor have one app-wide CSP, and a meta CSP can only tighten it, so on desktop 'no unsafe-eval in the main app' doesn't hold. How BotGuard makes its network calls under connect-src 'none' is unspecified.
- M1 is 'Phases 1–2', yet '1.11 is not required'.
issues.suggestion: Have 1.2 own a SandboxTransport interface plus a fake that 1.10 implements, or merge 1.10 into 1.2. Add 2.2 to 1.11's dependencies. Give the SABR rung its own done-when, such as N seconds of MediaSource playback. Specify how 1.11 isolates eval on Tauri and Capacitor: a separate window or webview with its own CSP, or accept 'unsafe-eval' there. Have the parent relay BotGuard's Create and GenerateIT calls. Define M1 as 'Phases 1–2 except 1.11'.

issues.issue: 1.12 can block M1 indefinitely. 2.8 depends on 1.12, and 1.12 is done only when the held-out set shows zero wrong Auto plays. The memo never says what happens if the gate fails; §6.3 implies Auto could simply stay off, but the plan doesn't say so. Labelling 200+ tracks 'with a hand review' also needs owner time that no stage accounts for.
issues.suggestion: Make 1.12 done once the labelled set and report are committed and CI replays them. Make the Auto band a setting that switches on only if the report passes, so M1 ships Suggest-only if it fails. Have 2.8 depend on the report, not on a pass. Name who does the hand review and estimate the time.

issues.issue: Free-tier problem the memo misses: Jamendo's Non-Commercial tier allows up to 35,000 API requests per month per client_id (developer.jamendo.com). FXM ships one public client_id to every user, and the Free-only tier, the 'prefer lossless' lookups (§7.1 step 4) and imports all call it. A modest user base would exhaust the monthly quota and break Jamendo for everyone at once. Making the ID overridable in Settings doesn't help users who never open Settings.
issues.suggestion: Call Jamendo only for explicit Jamendo searches or when 'prefer lossless' is on, and cache responses. Show a clear 'Jamendo quota used up; add your own client_id' state. Check Jamendo's API terms on shared IDs before shipping, and do the same for the shared Last.fm key.

issues.issue: The positioning rules are already broken in public text, and R.4's scope would not fix it. The develop README (public, and due to go out with the next release PR) says 'Play practically any song from YouTube Music, ad-free' and 'Download any track'. ARCHITECTURE.md's intro says 'download any track' and 'Spotify-quality recommendations'. R.4's scope covers only 'the notice section of README.md'. And 5.3 is told to 'follow the R.4 positioning rules now' while R.4 depends on 5.3.
issues.suggestion: Fix the README feature bullets and the ARCHITECTURE intro now. Widen R.4's scope to all public copy: README, docs intros, web app strings, extension descriptions and store listings. Split R.4 into the rules text (no dependencies, wave 1–2) and the legal pages, mirror and playbook (after 5.3).

issues.issue: Native Spotify cookie handling contradicts the memo's own rules. On Android, 6.2 keeps 'CapacitorHttp.request only as a stopgap', but Capacitor installs a process-wide CookieHandler backed by the WebView cookie jar (F10 verdicts). Every stopgap request therefore sends and stores WebView cookies, including sp_dc from the Spotify login WebView on any spotify.com call, which contradicts 'Isolate cookies on Android'. On desktop, §3.2 sends 'a Cookie header (needs unsafe-headers)' through plugin-http, which is a JS API, so sp_dc must pass through page JavaScript. That contradicts ARCHITECTURE §11: 'cookies never reach page JavaScript'.
issues.suggestion: Drop the CapacitorHttp stopgap, or clear CookieHandler.setDefault for it. On desktop, make the account-token call a Rust command that reads the keychain and returns only the token, so Spotify no longer needs unsafe-headers.

issues.issue:
Some content has no verified ad-free rung by default.
- Age-restricted videos generally need a signed-in client, and the default ladder (VISIONOS, then ANDROID itag 18) is cookieless. Bloomee #465 shows its chain failing on one.
- 'Made for kids' videos are routed to itag 18, but that is unverified: VISIONOS can't play them (yt-dlp #17871), and NewPipe 9ed62db says kids videos can't be played after it dropped the ANDROID client.
- Livestreams and premieres in Music + Video have no fixed file to probe and are often HLS-only.
'Practically any song' should state these exclusions.
issues.suggestion: Add explicit 'unavailable: age-restricted / made for kids / live' states, with fixtures. Test itag 18 on a made-for-kids ID before relying on it. Offer only the opt-in rungs (tv_samsung, the user's own Invidious instance) for these cases, and say so in the UI and docs.

issues.issue: The clean-room evidence doesn't cover the hashes FXM needs. The 5 plugin hashes found verbatim in Spotify's bundle are library and curation operations: applyCurations, fetchLibraryTracks, areEntitiesInLibrary, libraryV3 and isCurated. None of the read operations FXM uses is among them: searchDesktop, getTrack, fetchPlaylist, queryArtistOverview, queryArtistRelated, home, getAlbum. Unless they are re-sourced, those hashes would come from the AGPL plugin, against the §3.9 process. getAlbum was also never tested anonymously, even though albums are core.
issues.suggestion: Make 1.5 record every hash it needs from Spotify's own web-player chunks (chunk filename and fetch date) in R.4's clean-room log before coding starts. Add an anonymous getAlbum call to 1.5's live smoke test.

issues.issue:
The 'No change' list hides edits that are actually required.
- 1.6 still requires MusicBrainz calls 'with a descriptive User-Agent', which §7.3 says page JS cannot set.
- 2.6, rewritten in 97fe265, owns the Dexie match cache, but the memo's new cache rules (keyed by mode; band, userPinned and evidence stored; Suggest never saved as confirmed) are not assigned to it, and ARCHITECTURE §12 still keys the cache by ISRC.
- 8.5 appears in neither list.
- 4.2 falls under Decision 2 but isn't flagged.
- 4.2 and 4.5 assume ffmpeg.wasm is hosted on Pages, but Pages limits each asset to 25 MiB and the stock @ffmpeg/core 0.12.10 wasm is 32,232,419 bytes (about 30.7 MiB).
issues.suggestion: Move these to 'Modify': 1.6 (drop the UA requirement in browsers, keep 1 request/s), 2.6 (match-cache fields and key) and 4.2 (Decision 2; an audio-only LGPL build under 25 MiB). Place 8.5 in one of the lists. For extracting audio from itag 18 (4.5), use a JavaScript MP4 remux such as mp4box.js instead of ffmpeg.

issues.issue:
The ARCHITECTURE corrections in §11.7 are incomplete, and agents implement from ARCHITECTURE. These statements still contradict the memo:
- §1: 'Without the extension, only free sources play'.
- §3: 'a plain web page can't search YouTube or resolve streams'.
- The §5 diagram.
- §7.2: boolean capabilities.
- §11: the write-back plan, although 8.6 is being removed.
- D12: 'the only way to reach YouTube ... from a static page'.
- D16: '16/16'.
- D18: drops Invidious, which returns as opt-in rung 7.
The 5.3 site (Features.astro, Faq.astro) also says that without Connect the web app plays only free sources.
issues.suggestion: Add rows to §11.7 for §1, §5, §7.2, §11 (write-back), D12, D16 and D18. Add a 5.3 copy change that describes the Lite tier and marks it experimental.

issues.issue:
Two queue and mode behaviours are left unspecified.
(1) The memo changes Suggest from 'plays with a switcher' (revision 2) to 'plays only after an explicit user action', but doesn't say whether a Spotify playlist or radio queue stops, skips or plays when it reaches a Suggest-band track.
(2) Last.fm station items are described as 'YouTube IDs used directly'. In Music mode, each ID first needs an InnerTube call to read musicVideoType, and OMV/UGC items then need a video-to-song match. That costs request budget and conflicts with videos being hidden in Music mode.
Relatedly, Music mode plays Internet Archive, Jamendo and local tracks, and can substitute them when 'prefer lossless' is on. The owner defined Music as 'only YouTube Music catalog songs'.
issues.suggestion: Specify that queues skip Suggest items, marked 'needs review', with a one-tap batch review and an optional 'play best guesses' setting. In Music mode, send Last.fm IDs through classification and the video-to-song rule within the request budget, or use the stations only as artist/title seeds. Confirm with the owner whether non-YouTube sources may play in Music mode, or put them behind a separate toggle.

issues.issue: SponsorBlock is on by default in Music + Video and sends every played video ID to sponsor.ajay.app, which conflicts with FXM's 'no telemetry' stance. The memo also doesn't mention attribution for SponsorBlock's database, which is licensed CC BY-NC-SA.
issues.suggestion: Use the k-anonymity endpoint (/api/skipSegments/<sha256 prefix>), disclose the third-party service in Settings, and add attribution.
